anchorTrust.note: The tree heads of the test transparency log every R member's anchors are in, as a verifier holds them by a means other than a signature: a checkpoint it already witnessed. A transparency-log anchor validates as a hash commitment when its proof, an RFC 9162 TransItem of type inclusion_proof_v2 over the leaf SHA-256(0x00 || envelopeDigest), recomputes to one of these for its logId and treeSize; its time is that head's timestamp.

keyNote: PUBLISHED TEST KEYS, derived from fixed seeds in gen_vectors.py. The observer key signs every envelope. The agent key signs nothing: it is the key agent.signers names, so the commitment-key disjointness rule has something to be disjoint from.
note: One member per row of Appendix B of the draft, in the row's order; draftId is the row's identifier and parentDraftId its from column. The members after the last row carry draftSection: each tests a rule of that section that Appendix B carries no row for, and continues the identifier series of the rows beside it. A member carrying draftRevision is a row of that later revision's Appendix B, under the identifier it prints, and tests a rule that revision changes, so a reader conforming only to the draft named above may fail it. A member carrying aggregation lists the values of one input the decision depended on, as the producer held them: a producer's aggregation over those values must yield the entry the record carries. R1 to R9 are retained records: the file carries the envelope beside its retention entry, expected.verdict is the envelope's verdict, and expected.dating is the result of the dating check of Section 4.7.1, reported beside it and never folded into it. An accept or reject member is scored on expected.verdict. An indeterminate member is a row the draft leaves open: it carries no expected.verdict, and a verifier conforms on it by reaching any verdict its readings list. expected.codes are the reference reader's names for its first refusal, published so two implementations can compare where they stopped; the draft does not define them.
